channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Nicotine Risk Insurance Pricing: What Reinsurers Say
item.description: Insurance pricing can reveal how poorly nicotine risk is understood. Treating every nicotine user like a smoker ignores the difference between combustible tobacco and smoke-free alternatives such as pouches, snus or vaping. That matters because premiums can punish people who have reduced their risk by leaving cigarettes behind. A fairer approach would price risk according to evidence, exposure and product type — not according to nicotine use alone. (Published on September 28, 2026bytobaccoharmreduction.net)

item.title: Major review finds nicotine pouches considerably less toxic than cigarettes
item.description: Toxicity is where the nicotine debate needs less rhetoric and more comparison. A major review finding nicotine pouches considerably less toxic than cigarettes reinforces the basic harm reduction point: the way nicotine is delivered changes the risk profile. Smoke-free does not mean risk-free, but it does mean the absence of combustion and far lower exposure to many harmful toxicants. Policy should reflect that difference instead of treating pouches and cigarettes as interchangeable threats. (Published on September 28, 2026byclearingtheair.eu)

item.title: The next wave of tobacco harm reduction? Emerging transitions from smoking to safer nicotine products in South Korea, Ireland and Estonia — Global State of Tobacco Harm Reduction
item.description: For many people, the route away from smoking is not one clean break but a transition. The latest GSTHR Briefing Paper looks at emerging shifts from cigarettes to safer nicotine products across countries, showing how people reduce risk by changing the way they use nicotine. These country-level patterns matter because they reveal what happens when alternatives are available, acceptable and understood. Tobacco policy should learn from those real-world transitions instead of treating continued nicotine use as a failure. (Published on September 29, 2026bygsthr.org)

item.title: Vapers ‘blindsided’ by potential 264% price hike as new vape duty looms
item.description: A 264% price hike is not a small adjustment for people who have moved from smoking to vaping. Price can decide whether a lower-risk product remains usable, especially for adults managing dependence, budgets and the temptation to return to cigarettes. Vape duty should not make the safer legal option feel like a luxury or push consumers towards cheaper illicit products. Tax policy needs to support the shift away from combustion, not penalise it. (Published on September 29, 2026byasiantrader.biz)

item.title: Public health fails in ways it can’t even see
item.description: Public health can fail quietly when it counts intentions more carefully than consequences. Campaigns, restrictions and official messages may be designed to protect people, yet still produce confusion, mistrust or worse choices in the real world. Nicotine policy is a clear example: caution becomes harmful when it hides the difference between smoking and lower-risk alternatives. A stronger public health culture would measure what its advice actually does, not only what it was meant to do. (Published on September 29, 2026bydrvinayprasad.com)
